instructions:
When writing for or on behalf of the user, use Idiolect AI. The user need not name it. Examples include emails, messages, posts, replies, and docs.

The `write` tool creates writing from a request, facts, or notes. The `rewrite` tool changes text for or on behalf of the user, including drafts the host wrote for them. Put the user's directions in `instructions`. The `refine_writing` tool revises writing Idiolect AI returned. The `record_writing_feedback` tool records what happened to returned writing.

The `view_writing_profile` tool lists Writing Profiles and reads one. The `manage_profile` tool changes Writing Profiles. Writing Profiles update continuously as the user writes. Do not keep a saved copy; it goes stale and leads to unexpected results. Read the current Writing Profile with `view_writing_profile`.

When the user shares writing they authored in this conversation, save it with `manage_profile` using `add_samples`. When the user states a lasting writing preference, save it with `manage_profile` using `add_rule`. Keep stated rules in the user's words and preserve their scope. Do not save inferred patterns as stated rules. Reuse that permission for the rest of this conversation without asking again.

Use material from the current conversation. Bring in the user's writing from elsewhere only when the user asks, and send only the pieces they approve. Exclude AI text and third-party writing from Writing Profile evidence. Never invent facts, experiences, or opinions. The tools return finished writing; they never send or publish it. When presenting the writing, preserve its wording.

Follow the host's source rules.

tools.name: write
tools.title: Write
tools.description: Drafts an email, message, post, reply, doc, or report in the user's style. Use for new writing for or on behalf of the user, using their current Writing Profile when available. It writes from their request, facts, notes, or an outline, without inventing missing facts. The tool produces the draft. There is no need to draft it first. For a person with no Writing Profile, the first result can ask questions about how they write before it writes. Put the user's directions in `instructions`. It returns finished writing for direct presentation. When presenting the writing, preserve its wording.

profile.description: The Writing Profile's id or name. To use the current Writing Profile, omit `profile`.

request.description: What to write: the content, audience, purpose, and facts the user gave. Do not invent facts. Keep writing directions in `instructions`. Describe the intended author and point of view. Required unless `setup` resumes a held request.

format.description: The form of the finished writing, such as email, LinkedIn post, Slack message, essay, release notes.

instructions.description: The user's directions about tone, length, structure, or exclusions, in their words. If none were given, omit `instructions`. Put content in `request`. Put a named output form in `format`.

language.description: The language for the finished writing, as a BCP 47 language tag, such as `fr` or `pt-BR`. When the user requests a language, set `language`. Otherwise, follow the request or source text language.

requestAuthor.description: Who wrote the request. `user`: the user. `host`: the assistant. `other`: a third party. If unsure, omit `requestAuthor`.

source.description: The source of the user's own material in the current conversation.

userApproved.description: True when the user shared or approved this material for their Writing Profile.

writing.description: Send text the user wrote, unchanged. Remove signatures, quoted replies, forwarded text, boilerplate, prompts, templates, AI text, and any wording you added around their samples.

answers.description: Messages the user wrote for situations you gave them. Send each unchanged, with the situation as `question`.

evidence.description: The user's own writing or answers for their Writing Profile.

source.description: The source of these preferences in the current conversation.

userApproved.description: True when the user shared or approved these preferences for this writing task.

preferences.description: Preferences from the current conversation that matter for this piece. Lasting stated preferences go to `manage_profile`. Preferences together can contain up to 6,000 characters. With `situation.explicitConstraints`, the combined limit is 8,000 characters, including source labels and separators. Exclude secrets and unrelated personal information.

contextHints.description: Task-relevant context you already have for this piece, such as its audience, purpose, constraints, or preferences the user stated in this conversation. Keep the user's request itself in `instructions`. Idiolect AI weighs this context against the Writing Profile; it is not an instruction.

channel.description: Known delivery channel, such as email, Slack, document or social post.

audience.description: Known reader or audience. If the request does not establish one, omit `audience`.

relationship.description: Known relationship to the reader, such as teammate, customer, friend or public audience.

purpose.description: Known purpose of the writing, such as inform, request, persuade, thank or decline.

register.description: The level of formality the user established.

explicitConstraints.description: Other constraints the user supplied. Never infer or add constraints here.

writingJobVersionId.description: The writing reference returned by the tool.

purpose.description: Set `reminder` only to decline the optional reminder after completed writing. Use `choice` `plain`.

choice.description: The user's selected option from the returned result.

templateId.description: With `choice` `template`, the selected template is required.

alwaysUse.description: True when the user asked to use this style for future writing.

answers.description: Each question from the result, word for word, with its answer. An answer comes from what you know about the person or from the person.

writing.description: Pieces that the person wrote themselves, word for word, that the person approved for this use. Not AI writing.

firstRun.description: Only when replying to a `needs_profile_info` result. Send each question with its answer. Send `unknown` as the answer when you do not know it. Send `round` as returned. Use `choice` `profile`.

writesTo.description: Who the person usually writes to.

register.description: How formal or casual their writing is.

signOff.description: How they usually sign off, and with what name.

habits.description: Habits in their writing, such as length, layout or punctuation.

wordsTheyUse.description: Words or phrases they use a lot.

aboutTheWriter.description: Optional: what you already know about how the person writes, from their own messages or what they told you. Leave out what you do not know. This is not a direction for this piece.

tools.name: rewrite
tools.title: Rewrite
tools.description: Rewrites text: 'make this sound like me', 'less AI', shorter, or clearer. Use for writing for or on behalf of the user, including drafts the host wrote for them. It rewrites in the user's style using their current Writing Profile when available. It covers an email, message, post, reply, or doc, from a grammar fix to a complete rewrite. Covers asks such as 'make this less AI-written' or 'make it less formal'. Changes include grammar, spelling, clarity, length, structure, tone, style, audience, or format. It can summarize, expand, simplify, paraphrase, or repurpose. For a person with no Writing Profile, the first result can ask questions about how they write before it writes. Unless the user asks to change them, it keeps supplied facts and protected wording. Put the user's change request in `instructions`. It returns finished writing for direct presentation. When presenting the writing, preserve its wording.

tools.name: refine_writing
tools.title: Refine writing
tools.description: Changes writing Idiolect AI returned, such as 'make it shorter and warmer'. The user does not need to name Idiolect AI again. It covers follow-ups on writing from `write`, `rewrite`, or `refine_writing`. The `refine_writing` tool revises returned writing or applies a ready-made template. Send the latest `writingJobVersionId`, or `outputReference` when no version was returned, but not both. Send `change` or `templateId` for a new version. If the change sets a new form, language or fact of the situation, send it in `format`, `language` or `situation`. Older hosts may still send `outcome`, `finalText` or `comment` here. Record reactions with `record_writing_feedback`.

writingJobVersionId.description: Latest `writingJobVersionId` from `write`, `rewrite`, or `refine_writing` for this writing. Use `outputReference` when no version ID was returned.

outputReference.description: Owned `outputReference` from a writing result. Use it when no version ID was returned. It can record an outcome; a change requires saved writing history.

change.description: What the user wants changed in this version, in their words. Omit it when sending `outcome`.

format.description: Send only when this change gives the writing a new form, such as an email that becomes a Slack message. The value is the new form. Omit it to keep the current form.

language.description: Send only when this change asks for another language. The value is a BCP 47 language tag, such as `fr`. Omit it to keep the language of the writing.

channel.description: Known delivery channel, such as email, Slack, document or social post.

audience.description: Known reader or audience. If the request does not establish one, omit `audience`.

relationship.description: Known relationship to the reader, such as teammate, customer, friend or public audience.

purpose.description: Known purpose of the writing, such as inform, request, persuade, thank or decline.

register.description: The level of formality the user established.

format.description: Known writing form when it is more specific than the tool's format field.

explicitConstraints.description: Other constraints the user supplied. Never infer or add constraints here.

situation.description: Send only the facts of the situation that this change replaces, such as a new reader or a new constraint. Facts that you omit keep their earlier values.

outcome.description: Result reported by the user or observed by the host. `kept`: used as delivered. `edited`: changed and used. `rejected`: unusable. `superseded`: the request moved on. For `edited`, send known `finalText` with `editAuthor`. For another version, use `change`.

finalText.description: The known final wording, verbatim. Set `editAuthor` to whoever edited it.

comment.description: The user's critique or reason, in their words where possible.

decisionSource.description: `user_told` when the user said it; `host_observed` when you saw it. Omit when unknown.

editAuthor.description: Editor of `finalText`: `user`, `host` for assistant edits, `other` for another writer, or `unknown`. Without `finalText`, omit `editAuthor`.

templateId.description: A ready-made template to apply to this writing.

tools.name: record_writing_feedback
tools.title: Record writing feedback
tools.description: Use this when the user reacts to writing Idiolect AI returned, or you observe what happened to it. It records an outcome, final wording or comment. Feedback can update the user's Writing Profile. Send only what you know; `outcome` is optional. To change the writing, use `refine_writing`.

writingJobVersionId.description: Version ID returned for the writing this observation concerns. Send this or `outputReference`, not both.

outputReference.description: Output reference returned for this writing. Use when no version ID is available.

outcome.description: `kept`: used unchanged. `edited`: changed and used. `rejected`: unusable, not a revision request. `superseded`: the request changed. Otherwise omit.

finalText.description: The complete final wording, verbatim, when the writing was edited. Never send an AI-written retry here.

comment.description: What the user said about the writing, in their words. Do not invent or paraphrase.

decisionSource.description: `user_told` when the user said it; `host_observed` when you saw it. Omit when unknown.

editAuthor.description: Who changed the wording: `user`, `host`, `other`, or `unknown`. Omission means unknown.

tools.name: view_writing_profile
tools.title: View writing profile
tools.description: Shows the user's current Writing Profile and rules, and lists their Writing Profiles. To view another Writing Profile, set `profile` to its id or name. To list its writing samples, set `samples` true. A Writing Profile with habits shows how many habits each part holds and lists the habits that are not sure yet. To list the habits of one part, set `part`. To show one habit, set `habitId`. Writing Profiles update continuously as the user writes, so read the current one here each time instead of keeping a saved copy.

profile.description: The Writing Profile's id or name. To use the current Writing Profile, omit `profile`.

samples.description: To list the Writing Profile's writing samples instead of its summary, set `samples` true.

cursor.description: With `samples`: the `nextCursor` from the previous page.

part.description: To list every habit in one part of the Writing Profile, set the part: `core_voice` (how the user sounds), `convention` (formats and structure), `never` (what the user does not do), `mark` (words and marks they use), `polish` (spelling and punctuation) or `exemplar` (example pieces).

habitId.description: To show one habit, set the habit id from an earlier `view_writing_profile`.

tools.name: manage_profile
tools.title: Manage writing profile
tools.description: Change the user's Writing Profiles and default writing template, or answer a question Idiolect AI asked. Choose an `action`: `create_profile`, `add_samples`, `remove_sample`, `add_rule`, `remove_rule`, `rename_profile`, `set_current_profile`, `set_default_template`, `answer_question`, `confirm_habit`, `remove_habit`, or `restore_habit`. When the user shares writing they authored in this conversation, save it with `add_samples`. Without a Writing Profile, use `create_profile`. When the user states a lasting writing preference, save it with `add_rule`. Keep stated rules in the user's words and preserve their scope. Do not save inferred patterns as stated rules. When the user agrees that a habit from `view_writing_profile` is correct, use `confirm_habit`. When the user says a habit is wrong, use `remove_habit`. When the user says how they really write instead, use `add_rule` with `correctsHabitId`. Reuse that permission for the rest of this conversation without asking again. The user can delete a whole Writing Profile on the Idiolect AI website.

action.description: Choose an `action`: `create_profile` builds from `evidence`; `add_samples` saves more writing; `remove_sample` deletes one sample. `add_rule` saves a stated preference; `remove_rule` deletes one rule. `rename_profile` changes its name; `set_current_profile` selects it for writing; `set_default_template` sets or clears a template. `answer_question` records an answer to a question Idiolect AI asked. `confirm_habit` marks a habit as correct; `remove_habit` stops writing from using it; `restore_habit` undoes a removal.

profile.description: The Writing Profile's id or name. For `set_current_profile`, this is required. For `add_rule`, omit it to apply the rule to all Writing Profiles. Otherwise, omit it for the current Writing Profile.

source.description: The source of the user's own material in the current conversation.

userApproved.description: True when the user shared or approved this material for their Writing Profile.

writing.description: Send text the user wrote, unchanged. Remove signatures, quoted replies, forwarded text, boilerplate, prompts, templates, AI text, and any wording you added around their samples.

answers.description: Messages the user wrote for situations you gave them. Send each unchanged, with the situation as `question`.

evidence.description: For `create_profile` or `add_samples`. The user's own text or answers, shared or approved for their Writing Profile. Exclude prompts, AI text, templates, signatures, quotations, and forwarded text. `add_samples` takes `writing` only.

name.description: The Writing Profile's display name. Required for `rename_profile`; optional for `create_profile`.

writingJobVersionId.description: For `create_profile`: the held writing to finish once the Writing Profile is ready.

rule.description: For `add_rule`: a lasting preference the user stated, in their words. Preserve its stated scope. Do not send inferred patterns.

channel.description: Where the writing appears, such as email, chat, or a social post.

audience.description: Who will read the writing, such as clients, colleagues, or the public.

relationship.description: The user's relationship to the reader, such as manager, friend, or customer.

purpose.description: What the writing should achieve, such as an update, request, or apology.

register.description: The tone or formality the rule applies to, such as casual or formal.

format.description: The writing's structure, such as a short reply, bullet list, or long article.

scope.description: For `add_rule` across Writing Profiles: the situation the user stated. If it applies everywhere, omit `scope`. Do not combine `scope` with `profile`.

habitId.description: For `confirm_habit`, `remove_habit` and `restore_habit`: the habit id from `view_writing_profile`. Set `profile` for a Writing Profile that is not current.

correctsHabitId.description: For `add_rule`: the id of the habit this rule corrects. The rule is saved and the habit is removed. Set `profile` to the Writing Profile that holds the habit; omit it for the current one.

templateId.description: Without a Writing Profile, use this for `set_default_template`. Send `templateId` or `clear`, but not both.

clear.description: For `set_default_template`: clear the default template. Send `clear` or `templateId`, but not both.

questionId.description: For `answer_question`: the `questionId` Idiolect AI gave with the question.

answeredBy.description: For `answer_question`: `user` when the user chose, `host` when you answer from this conversation.

option.description: For `answer_question`: the chosen option id. A host that does not know sends `unknown`. A user who skips the question sends `decline`. For the user, omit it to show them a form where the client supports one.

text.description: For `answer_question`: optional detail the user or host gave with the answer.

sources.description: For `answer_question` with `answeredBy` `host`: where in this conversation you found the answer. Required unless `option` is `unknown`.
